architecture_selection_rule_item_18.rule: Multi-objective gate, NOT a single composite score (this is itself the fix for PHASE2_REOPEN_ANALYSIS.md's finding that the original composite hid the entity regression). A candidate architecture (which may be a hybrid: e.g. Candidate A/dictionary-based entity extraction + Candidate B's intent/constraint/source handling) is acceptable ONLY if ALL of the following hold simultaneously on the dev split, each reported individually, then reconfirmed once on the untouched test split at the very end:
gates: Entity F1 (micro) does not materially regress from the strongest verified Phase-2 baseline (0.886, Candidate A dev) - 'materially' defined as no more than 2 points absolute, matching this benchmark's n=45-105 confidence-interval scale; any larger gap must be quantitatively explained, not waived.
Normalization: fabricated_id_count == 0 always; accuracy@1 reported with n.

Intent: no systematic (>=80% of a class's examples) single-class confusion remains in the confusion matrix; every one of the 8 query-time classes has measurable, non-zero support and a non-zero recall attempt.

Constraints: no individual constraint field's F1 is 'systematically broken' (defined as F1 < 0.3 with support >= 5); phase/status fields specifically must round-trip canonicalize_trial_phase/canonicalize_trial_status correctly, verified by tests/test_nlu.py.
Structured output: schema-parse success rate measured and reported (not assumed 100%); empty responses get one deterministic retry then an explicit NLU_FAILURE outcome, never fabricated content.
Latency: P50 appropriate for an interactive upstream stage (target: P50 well under 10s; P95 reported honestly even if it doesn't hit that target, with a stated reason).
Ambiguity: gene/protein/target multi-role cases use semantic_roles rather than forced single-type certainty; genuinely ambiguous queries set AmbiguityState.is_ambiguous=true rather than guessing.
architecture_selection_rule_item_18.explicitly_allowed: A hybrid/decomposed final architecture (best entity extractor + best intent/constraint component + deterministic normalization/canonicalization + a validated merge step) if no single architecture clears every gate above. This is the current working hypothesis pending the dev_rerun_b_entitytype_constraintfield results.
architecture_selection_rule_item_18.not_yet_decided: Whether Candidate A's entity extraction is actually reusable/mergeable with Candidate B's intent/constraint/source output, or whether Candidate B's entity extraction can close the gap on its own now that the B/G and canonicalization fixes are in - this is exactly what the in-progress dev rerun is measuring before any hybrid-architecture code is written.
